paragraphs.parakeet: If you could move to any country tomorrow, would you leave yours? Let's find out where people want out and where they want in, starting with the biggest magnet on the planet, Canada.
paragraphs.whisper: If you could move to any country tomorrow, would you leave yours? Let's find out where people want out and where they want in, starting with the biggest magnet on the planet, Canada.

paragraphs.parakeet: Green Magnet instantly. Gallup compares how many people want to move in with how many want to move out and Canada scores plus 225%. In theory, its adult population would more than triple. Bring a warm coat.

paragraphs.parakeet: Right below the USA, still the world's number one dream. 15% of everyone who wants to emigrate picks America first. But that's the lowest share in nearly two decades, and one in five Americans now say they'd like to leave themselves.

paragraphs.parakeet: Now south where the arrows flip. Mexico 20% won out. Guatemala 32. Belize is a quiet exception. By UN estimates more people arrive than leave. Then Honduras the hot spot. Half of all adults wanted to leave in 2023 though by 2025 that fell to 35. Next door, El Salvador at 34 and Nicaragua at 19.

paragraphs.parakeet: Costa Rica 30. Panama 21. Even the canal can't keep everyone. Into the Caribbean, Jamaica loses more people than it gains. Cuba is the big one. In an independent 2023 poll, more than half said they want to leave the island and the U.S. now partially suspends visas for Cubans. The Bahamas, sun, see, and most people staying put.

paragraphs.parakeet: Haiti is where wanting and leaving collide. In Gallup's 2015-2017 survey, 63% wanted out, and today the U.S. fully suspends entry for Haitians. Wanting to go isn't the same as being let in. Dominican Republic, 46%. Trinidad and Tobago mostly staying.

paragraphs.parakeet: Next stop, South America. Venezuela, 27%, partly because so many have already gone. The UN estimates it lost about 15 people per thousand every year from 2019 to 2023. Colombia, 36. Ecuador, 49, nearly half. Peru, 42. Bolivia, 36. Down south, Chile, 35 and Argentina 34. Uruguay, 25. Paraguay is the calm one, just 17. Brazil, the giant, 23. Suriname mostly staying, and Guyana, small but losing people fast by UN estimates.

Across the Atlantic and the map turns green. Portugal plus 125. Spain plus 74. France plus 44. The UK is still a top dream destination, picked by 4% of would-be migrants worldwide, even though nearly a quarter of Brits tell one poll they are thinking about moving abroad. Ireland plus 138, the comeback kid. In 2015 to 2017, it was only plus 48.

paragraphs.parakeet: Iceland and Norway more arrivals than departures by UN estimates. Sweden plus 91, Finland plus 97, Denmark plus 129. Cold winters, warm numbers. The Netherlands plus 43, Belgium plus 48, and tiny Luxembourg plus 150. Germany plus 53. Switzerland more in and out. Austria plus 83. And Italy plus 25 when 10 years ago it was negative.

paragraphs.parakeet: Next stop the east where the green fades. Slovenia plus 8, Croatia plus 7 nearly balanced. Then the Balkans. Bosnia, 38% have considered leaving. Serbia and Montenegro, 40-50% in the Balkan barometer. Albania was at 60% in Gallup's 2015 to 2017 count. North Macedonia, 35%. Greece and Bulgaria almost even.

paragraphs.parakeet: Romania minus 22 and Hungary minus 24 the lowest score in the EU. Slovakia and Czechia slightly negative. Poland minus 5. Lithuania and Latvia minus 15 each. Estonia minus 6. Belarus and Moldova losing people by UN estimates. And Ukraine, after years of war, 21% say they would leave if the borders fully opened.

paragraphs.parakeet: Next stop Russia. Only 9% want to move abroad for good, the lowest Levada has ever recorded. Georgia also 9. Armenia 22. Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, roughly balanced by UN estimates. Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan slightly more arrivals. And Afghanistan. After the Taliban returned, 53% wanted to leave. A Gallup record. Its passport opens just 22 countries without a visa, the weakest on earth, and the US has fully banned entry.

Next stop the Middle East. Iran a third want to emigrate and the US travel ban now covers it completely. Iraq 35%. Kuwait just 16. Then the Gulf flips everything. Bahrain balanced. Qatar the UAE and Oman pull people in and the UAE's net migration is about 20 people per thousand a year. Yemen war a weak passport and a full US ban. Saudi Arabia a top 10 dream destination worldwide.

Three out of four adults would leave if they could and Sierra Leone is now under a full US entry ban. Ivory Coast 29. Mali and Burkina Faso only 12 each, the lowest in Africa.

paragraphs.parakeet: Across the Indian Ocean. Sri Lanka losing a few people by UN estimates. India, just 4% told Gallup International they'd rather live in another country. Pakistan is the twist. Nepal and Bangladesh losing people too with passports among the 10 weakest. Bhutan balanced.

paragraphs.parakeet: So here's the final map. 16 magnets, 16 countries with more people moving in, 47 where most people stay, 52 where many want out, 26 where it's close to half or more, and 2 where people simply can't leave. And notice the pattern. The places people most want to leave often have the passports that open the fewest doors. So, where would you go? Tell us in the comments.
